He gathered firewood and brush,
kindled a fire beneath him,
and the smoke and flames gradually grew fierce.
The withered tree then caught fire.
At that time, among the merchants in the caravan, there was a trader who,
after the second watch of the night had passed, [saw this].
While he recited the Abhidharma Piṭaka,
various bats gathered together and, though distressed by the fire,
listened to his excellent sound of the Dharma.
He endured it and did not leave;
thereupon his life came to an end,
and he was reborn according to his karma.
Both attained human bodies;
they left their homes to study the teachings of the Hīnayāna,
being clever and of sharp intelligence.
He also realized the fruits of sainthood.
He lived near King Kaniṣka and was a contemporary of the Venerable Pārśva.
He convened five hundred sages in the kingdom of Kaśmīra to compose the *Vibhāṣā-śāstra*.
These were none other than five hundred bats from within that withered tree.

13. The Thirteenth Account of a Mouse Hearing the Vinaya Piṭaka: A Response through Spiritual Resonance. Formerly, at the monastery of the Arhat Madhyāntika in the kingdom of Kaśmīra, there was a mouse. [The account continues: Once, while the monks were reciting the Vinaya Piṭaka, the sound reached the ears of this mouse. Having heard it, he developed a deep faith and subsequently passed away. By virtue of that karmic cause, he was reborn in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven as a devaputra named Vinayadharasvara (Sound-Holding of the Vinaya). He possessed a divine body of golden hue and was endowed with the five supernormal powers. One day, he descended to the Jeta Grove to pay homage to the Buddha. At that time, the World-Honored One was preaching the Dharma to the great assembly. The devaputra approached the Buddha, bowed his head to the ground, and withdrew to sit to one side. He then addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, in my past life I was a mouse dwelling in the monastery of the Arhat Madhyāntika in the kingdom of Kaśmīra. While the monks were reciting the Vinaya Piṭaka, I happened to hear it. Because of that single act of hearing the Dharma, I have now been born in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven. Having spoken thus, he further requested the Buddha to preach the Dharma for him. The Buddha then preached the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* for him. Upon hearing it, the devaputra attained the stage of Non-Retrogression (*avaivartika*). Thereafter, he returned to his celestial abode. This is the thirteenth account of a mouse hearing the Vinaya Piṭaka.
There was an arhat who possessed the three insights and six supernormal powers with utter clarity,
and who had mastered the Three Piṭakas and the twelve divisions of the teachings.
Among them, his observance of the precepts was pure and lofty;
he was just like Upāli in the world,
constantly admonishing his disciples, saying:
"You all should diligently practice and study the precepts.
Why is this? Because in the past, when I was still at the stage of an ordinary person,"
Due to his evil karma, he received the body of a rat and dwelt within a stone cave.
At that time, there was a bhikṣu.
I heard that he stayed overnight in a cave reciting the Vinaya Piṭaka;
by virtue of this root of goodness, he received a human body.
He attained arhatship,
his precepts being pure and refined.
If even one in the body of a mouse can thus hear and master the Vinaya Piṭaka, how much more so for a human being!
How much more so for those who practice with faith! 14.

The Fourteenth Account of Miraculous Responses from Upholding the Vinaya Piṭaka. The text concerning the miraculous responses from upholding the Vinaya Piṭaka is as follows: Formerly, at the Kuvinda Vihāra in the kingdom of Kaśmīra...
There were two bhikṣus:
one who upheld the Vinaya Piṭaka,
and one who upheld the Abhidharma Piṭaka.
Everyone provided the Vinaya Master with the finest and most exquisite food.
During the night, devas and humans arrived to pay homage to the bhikṣu who upheld the Vinaya.
For more than a month, he did not pay homage to the bhikṣu who upholds the treatises. After this period,
the bhikṣu who upholds the treatises...
Harboring resentment and anger,
the deva rebuked him, saying,
"The precepts open the way to the human and heavenly realms."
Even unto the path to Nirvana;
for these reasons,
gods and humans hold those who recite it in high esteem.
One should not feel regret.
At that time, the bhikṣu who upholds the treatises shall diligently practice the preservation of the Vinaya Piṭaka.
Both attained the first fruit [of the path].
At that time, a deity made offerings to the two bhikṣus. 15.

The Fifteenth Account of the Miraculous Response of the Extinction of Sin through Śākyamuni’s Past Acquisition of One Case of the Mahāsannipāta Sūtra. The account of the miraculous response of the extinction of sin through Śākyamuni’s past acquisition of one case of the *Mahāsannipāta-sūtra* appears in the *Jifa yueshe ku tuoluoni jing* (Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī for Collecting the Joy of the Dharma and Abandoning Suffering).
This is a separate stream from within the Mahāsannipāta Sūtra. In the past, during incalculable kalpas,
when Śākyamuni was still an ordinary person,
he was named Ceta in the kingdom of Kāruṇya.
Engaging in the livelihood of a merchant and peddler,
one acts with falsehood and unreality,
committing various evil deeds.
He harmed his father and loved his mother;
this continued for several years until all the people throughout the land became aware of it.
He raised his voice and cried out, "Stop!
Do not harm my father or my beloved mother!
At that moment, he reflected:
No different from a beast,
he then leaped over the city wall at night and fled toward a deep marsh.
King Viśāla addressed the people of the kingdom, saying:
"This man is furthermore lustful, deluded, and devoid of the Way."
"To whoever is able to obtain it,
I shall grant a generous reward of precious goods. Thus,
the people of the country each accepted the challenge.
Desiring to capture his person,
he immediately left the country and became a śramaṇa in another land.
He sat in meditation and studied the Way,
weeping day and night for a full thirty-seven years.
Because of the obstacle of the five heinous crimes,
his mind could not attain [liberation] for thirty-seven years while remaining in a mountain cave.
Raising his voice, he wept and lamented with deep sorrow.
Descending into the cave to beg for food,
he found a large alms bowl on the path.
Within it was a single case containing a scripture;
there were no other scriptures,
only the *Mahāsaṃnipāta-dharmārāma-duḥkhaprahāṇa-dhāraṇī-sūtra*.
This sutra can eliminate the great sins of the five heinous acts and the cycle of birth and death for ten billion kalpas.
If there are those who receive, uphold, read, and recite it,
they shall never fall into the three miserable realms.
Why is this? Because it has been spoken by Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
At that time, having obtained this sutra, [one should practice accordingly].
He immediately ceased begging for alms and joyfully proceeded toward his cave,
where he burned incense and paid homage.
Weeping with compassion,
he praised and venerated [the deity]. He practiced recitation within a cave for one year before finally succeeding.
Due to the obstruction of karmic offenses,
one cannot enter the state of mind [of the practitioner] and practice for several more years until one attains unimpeded flight.
One beholds the Buddhas of the ten directions.
Furthermore, there are practitioners who practice according to the Dharma, and so forth.

16. The Response of Rebirth in the Pure Land of the Bhikṣu Daoru of Bingzhou through Merely Hearing the Names of the Vaipulya Sūtras. There was a bhikṣu in Bingzhou named Daoru. He merely heard the names of the Vaipulya sūtras and was thereby moved by a spiritual response leading to rebirth in the Pure Land. There was a bhikṣu in Bingzhou...
It is named Daoru (Tathatā).
Among the people of this province,
those aged seven years and above...
Although many understand the practice of mindfulness of the Buddha,
this bhikṣu neither cultivates mindfulness of the Buddha nor maintains the precepts.
He kept impure things;
his body committed offenses which he did not repent.
He lived to the age of sixty-one.
He suddenly suffered a stroke and died after more than a month;
he began to revive only on the third day.
"Your daily activities are light and comfortable;
your illness has been completely cured. When I first died, I saw Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta coming toward me."
He instructed, exhorted, benefited, and gladdened them, saying:
"You have not cultivated the practices for the Pure Land;
you have merely heard the names of the Mahāyāna Vaipulya sūtras in their twelve divisions."
By these causes and conditions,
the stains of their offenses have become thin and slight;
thus they have come from afar as shadows and echoes.
With his remaining lifespan not yet exhausted,
after twelve years he will be reborn in the Pure Land.
He immediately joined his palms and wept until he regained consciousness;
thereafter, he relinquished all his possessions to produce the Mahāvaipulya Mahāsannipāta Sūtra.
He concurrently practiced the recitation of the Buddha's name.
On the fifteenth day of the first month in the twelfth year, he passed away;
at that time, music was heard within his chamber.
Heavenly flowers fell as rain;
this was witnessed and heard by those present.

17. The Seventeenth Case: The Miraculous Response of Receiving Prophecies by the Two Monks Tánróng and Sēngdì While Practicing the Fangděng Repentance Method. Recorded from the *Biographies of Eminent Monks of the Tang* (*Táng Gāosēng Zhuàn*). Śramaṇa Tánróng of Fǎzhù Temple in Lù Prefecture during the Tang Dynasty.
In the seventh year of the Zhenguan era,
at the request of the lay devotees Chang Ningbao and others,
he performed the Fangdeng Repentance Rite at Fazhu Temple.
On the fourteenth day of the seventh month,
there was a śramaṇa named Sengding from this temple,
whose observance of the precepts was pure and eminent.
Within the site of enlightenment,
he beheld a great radiance;
five colors arose in alternation, ascending and descending.
Within it were seven Buddhas,
whose physical marks and signs were extraordinary;
they spoke to the monk Dingyun, saying:
I, the Tathāgata Vipaśyin, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha,
have come to bear witness because your transgressions have been extinguished;
however, I am not your original teacher.
He did not grant him a prophecy.
In this manner, all six buddhas spoke these same words.
The last buddha said:
"I am your original teacher, Śākyamuni.
I have come to bestow this prediction upon you so that your transgressions may be extinguished.
Tanrong is the excellent condition for the eradication of your offenses."
In this Bhadrakalpa,
you shall be named Samantaprasanna Buddha;
your physical vessel is pure.
"In the future, you shall become a Buddha,
also named Puming (Universal Radiance).
Such a manifestation of response and the elicitation of auspicious omens are indeed difficult to hear of with faith."

18. The Eighteenth Account of Miraculous Responses to the Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa Sūtra as Expounded by the Great Master Zhiyi of the Sui Dynasty. The accounts of miraculous responses to the Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa Sūtra as expounded by the Great Master Zhiyi of the Sui Dynasty appear in the *Chuan* (Biographies) and the *Ruìyìng Chuan* (Records of Auspicious Responses). Regarding the Great Master Zhiyi of the Sui Dynasty:
His taboo name was Zhiyi;
his surname was Chen, and he was a native of Yingchuan.
At the time of his birth, a mountain sprang up from the earth, which was named Daxian.
At the time of his passing, the mountain immediately sank away,
becoming the Great Xian Lake.
There he lectured on the Vimalakīrti Sūtra.
Next, suddenly three jeweled stairways were seen descending from the sky.
The entire assembly of Akṣobhya Buddha’s land appeared there,
solemn and majestic.
Ten Brahmā-monks,
holding incense burners, entered the hall and circumambulated Zhiyi three times.
Eulogy: Excellent, Zhiyi!
You have profoundly realized the Buddha’s intent; my coming as a shadow and echo has produced such a response. 19.

The Response of Shi Puming upon Reciting the Vimalakīrti Sūtra, the Nineteenth [Chapter]. The Response of Shi Puming upon Reciting the Vimalakīrti Sūtra, as recorded in the *Liang Dynasty Biographies of Eminent Monks*: Shi Puming was a monk of Linzi during the Song dynasty.
He recited the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* and the *Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa-sūtra*.
While reciting the *Vimalakīrti-sūtra*,
he heard a voice from the air proclaiming his joy.
Furthermore, he was skilled in efficacious mantras;
all whom he rescued were healed.
There was a man of noble status named Wang Daozhen.
His wife was ill, and he requested Ming to enter the inner quarters.
The woman then fell into a swoon.
Suddenly, she saw a creature resembling a wild cat, several feet in length, and so forth.

20. The Response of the Scribe Who Transcribed the Vimalakīrti Sūtra in Shanyin, Kuaiji. New Record of the Response of the Scribe Who Transcribed the Vimalakīrti Sūtra in Shanyin, Kuaiji. There was a scribe in Shanyin County, Kuaiji.
He lost his family name and personal name,
and his body suffered from a slight ailment;
he then made a vow to transcribe the Vimalakīrti Sūtra.
At the beginning of the night when he first established the title,
he dreamed of a celestial maiden who rubbed the scholar’s body; upon waking from the dream, [he composed the work].
The illness vanished instantly;
he further developed faith and completed the entire text of one section.
Furthermore, he made a vow to transcribe one copy for the sake of his deceased relatives.
When he reached the "Inquiry after Illness" chapter,
he suddenly dreamed of a celestial being riding upon the clouds.
Arriving at his dwelling, he said,
"I am your father;
it is because of my evil karma [that I have come to this]."
"You have fallen into the Dark Hell.
You have composed a sutra for us;
its radiance illuminates our bodies."
Having ceased his suffering, he was reborn in heaven; out of joy,
he came to inform [the Buddha] of the cause.
He asked again,
"I do not know where my mother is.
He replied, "Your mother, due to her attachment to wealth, has fallen among the hungry ghosts."
"Transcribe the 'Buddhakṣetra-parivarta';
you shall immediately leave suffering behind and be born in the Land of No-Trembling.
I, too, shall soon be born there."
Having diligently completed the transcription,
he wept upon waking from his dream.
He then transcribed another complete set and made offerings to it.
Furthermore, in a dream, there was an official in unusual attire who approached holding a banner and announced:
"The King of Dharma, Yama, has issued a summons."
Because you have transcribed the Vimalakīrti Sūtra,
you shall be born in the Buddha-field of Suvarṇabāhu.
The King granted you twenty years of life;
strive diligently and do not be indolent.
You shall pass away at the age of seventy-nine.
His body was golden in color;
those who saw him all thought it was merely a manifestation of a Buddha from the Golden Grain (Suvarṇakaṇa) Buddha-land. 21.

The Response of Dharma-Master Fazu Preaching the Śūraṅgama Sūtra for King Yama, Number Twenty-One. Regarding the response of Dharma-Master Fazu preaching the Śūraṅgama Sūtra for King Yama, it appears in the *Biographies* (Chuan): "Fazu, whose courtesy name was Boyuan."
A native of Henei,
he subsequently constructed a vihāra in Chang’an.
While he was making the study and recitation of the Śūraṅgama Sūtra his primary occupation,
there was a man surnamed Li and named Tong.
It is said that after dying and reviving,
he saw Dharma Master Zu at the abode of King Yama,
where the Master was expounding the Śūraṅgama Sūtra for the king.
Countless sinful beings,
upon hearing the sound of their teacher’s preaching,
were reborn in the second heaven.
He himself said:
"Upon the completion of this lecture, I shall be reborn in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven.
If the gods of that heaven hear this sutra..."
One attains the merit of non-retrogression. 22.

The Second-Twelfth Account of the Miraculous Response of Rainfall During Master Yun’s Lecture on the Śrīmālā Sūtra at Guangzhai Temple. Regarding the miraculous response of rainfall during Master Yun’s lecture on the Śrīmālā Sūtra at Guangzhai Temple, as recorded in the *Biographies*: Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty wished to pray for rain.
Master Zhi said,
"If you wish to invite Master Yun of Guangzhai Temple to lecture on the Śrīmālā-sūtra, then do so immediately;
once the rain falls, all shall receive its nourishment and be sufficiently satisfied."

23. The Twenty-third Account of the Poor Woman Who Recited the Śrīmālā-sūtra and Manifested as the Empress: A Response to the Sacred. This account of the poor woman who recited the Śrīmālā-sūtra and manifested as the Empress is recorded in the *Sanbao ji* (Records of the Three Jewels). Formerly, three hundred years after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa...
In the kingdom of Aśvaja, there was a poor woman who had no relatives at all;
she gathered firewood to sustain her life.
During her leisure time, she received and upheld the Śrīmālā-sūtra;
the poor woman, having gathered firewood, entered the mountains again and,
her body being exhausted, was unable to return.
He was lying down in the mountains reciting the sutras.
At that time, the king went out on a hunting expedition and entered the mountains.
Suddenly he saw this woman,
whose body was covered by a cloud;
the king marveled at this and drew near to look.
The upright woman returned to the palace in joy and was established as the Queen.
In that land, this scripture has long been discontinued and no longer practiced;
it is at such a time that seekers of the Dharma shall emerge once again to restore it.
In this regard, one obtains the original text of this sutra. 24.

The Response of Chan Master Daozhen’s Recitation of the Amitābha Sūtra and Rebirth in the Pure Land, Number Twenty-Four. The response concerning Chan Master Daozhen’s recitation of the *Amitābha Sūtra* and his rebirth in the Pure Land appears in the *Ruìyìng Zhuàn* (Account of Auspicious Responses) and other texts. Daozhen of the Liang Dynasty.
While practicing the mindfulness of the Buddha through the visualization of water, he dreamed of water;
a hundred people were aboard a boat,
wishing to travel westward and seeking a place to board.
The people on the boat would not listen.
Fajin said,
"I have spent my entire life cultivating the karma for the Western Paradise."
"Why did you not allow it?
The man on the boat replied,
"The Master has not yet recited the Amitābha Sūtra."
They also prepared a bathhouse;
thereupon, the boatmen set out all at once,
but they were unable to depart.
She woke from her weeping and then recited sutras and bathed the monks.
At another time, she again had a dream.
A person from the Single Vehicle Silver Tower raised their hand and said:
"Your karma is now complete; you may employ your mind as you see fit."
Therefore, I have come to inform you that you will certainly be reborn in the Western Pure Land at the end of this life.
This was said on the night of his passing.
The mountain peak appeared as if dozens of torches were blazing,
and a wondrous fragrance filled the temple.
After his passing, [relics] were found within the scripture case.
I have obtained the testament he left during his lifetime. 25.

The Twenty-fifth Account of Dharma Master Tanluan’s Response to the *Contemplation Sutra* Regarding Rebirth in the Pure Land. The Twenty-fifth Account of Dharma Master Tanluan’s Response to the *Contemplation Sutra* regarding rebirth in the Pure Land is identical in text to that of Dharma Master Tanluan of the Qi Dynasty.
He obtained ten fascicles of the *Xianjing* (Scripture of the Immortals) from this land and intended to visit Tao Hongjing to study the arts of transcendence.
Later, he encountered the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhidharma, who asked him:
"In the Buddha-dharma, there is a method for longevity and immortality;
is it superior to the *xián jīng* (immortal scriptures) of this land?
The Tripiṭaka Master spat on the ground and said in alarm:
Where in this world is there a method for long life and immortality?
Even if one were to attain an extended lifespan,
when the years are exhausted, one must still fall into the three realms of existence.
He then presented the *Amitāyurdhyāna-sūtra* to Ryō, saying,
"This is the method of the Great Sage."
Relying upon this, practice accordingly;
you shall long attain liberation and forever depart from birth and death.
Luán then required fire and consequently burned the immortal scriptures.
Suddenly, in the middle of the night—
Moved by the verses spoken by Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna,
he then knew his life had come to an end;
he personally took up an incense burner and faced west.
He practiced the recollection of the Buddha and then passed away.
He heard music from the west coming through the air,
and returned in an instant.

26. The Response of the Monk Senggan from Bingzhou Who Attained Rebirth in the Pure Land through Reciting and Upholding the *Contemplation Sūtra* and the *Amitābha Sūtra*, Part Twenty-Six. From the New Record of Responses of Monks from Bingzhou Who Attained Rebirth in the Pure Land through Reciting and Upholding the *Contemplation Sūtra* and the *Amitābha Sūtra*: There was a bhikṣu in Bingzhou named Senggan.
Taking the *Sukhāvatīvyūha-sūtra* and the *Amitābha-sūtra* as his practice,
he was moved by a dream in which he saw himself growing wings;
with his left hand, he held the text of the *Sukhāvatīvyūha-sūtra*.
The above is the text of the *Amitābha Sūtra*.
Because my body still feels somewhat heavy when wishing to levitate,
I have recited both sūtras with full awareness.
Three years later, in a dream:
his wings having grown full,
he wished to fly, yet felt slightly light.
After another two years,
he had a dream in which his body became light and he soared through the void without obstruction;
he then pointed toward the west and flew away.
Upon reaching the Land of Ultimate Bliss,
there will be one Buddha and two Bodhisattvas;
this is due to the power of your recitation of the sutra.
Having reached the borderlands of Sukhāvatī,
you must return to Sahā quickly.
Recite four hundred and eighty fascicles every day for one thousand days.
Thereafter, he was reborn in a superior realm.
As he had been instructed, he practiced while awake as if in a dream for three years until his end.
At the place where he lay, nine stalks of lotus flowers suddenly sprang forth.
It did not wither or fall for seven days. 27. The Twenty-seventh Response:

A Small Kingdom in Western India Attained Peace with a Rival Nation through the Recitation of the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-sūtra*. This account of how a small kingdom in Western India attained peace with a hostile nation through the recitation of the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-sūtra* appears in the *Kaiyuan lu* and the *Moting zhuan*. There was once a small kingdom in Western India.
He requested the Venerable Mātanga to preach the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-sūtra*.
Shortly thereafter, a master from a neighboring kingdom arrived.
As they were about to enter the territory,
they were suddenly obstructed by affairs;
the troops could not advance.
The military forces of that country possessed only extraordinary arts;
he secretly dispatched an envoy to observe them.
He saw only the ministers sitting at ease,
all listening together to the Mahāyāna sūtra he was expounding,
which elucidated the methods for protecting the nation according to the Dharma of the Earth-Ruling Devas (Mahīśvaras).
Thereupon, that country requested peace and sought the Dharma;
both attained security and stability. 28.

A Record of Miraculous Responses from the Lecture on the *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra* by a Monk from China in Central India, Number Twenty-Eight. This account of miraculous responses from the lecture on the *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra* by a monk from China in Central India appears in the *Xiguo zhuan* (Records from Western Regions). There was a kingdom in Central India...
It was named Puṇḍravardhana.
Eight hundred years after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata,
the land became overgrown with weeds and the five grains failed to ripen.
The king, his ministers, and the common people suffer from famine;
pestilence spreads abroad,
and those who die of unnatural causes fill the roads.
The king asked his ministers,
"By what means can this suffering be alleviated?
The wise minister addressed the king, saying:
"To eliminate the demonic calamities of the state,
nothing is superior to the Buddhist scriptures.
Your Majesty should therefore practice the Buddha's teachings."
The king asked,
"Which sūtra?
The minister replied:
Formerly, in the kingdom of Magadha, Jīvaka,
who was difficult to rely upon, lectured on the *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*, the King of Sutras. The king,
intending to lecture and listen to that scripture, [prepared for it].
The King immediately invited the Dharma Master.
During one summer retreat, he lectured on the sutras five times.
At that time, he dreamed of various youths.
He took up a bamboo staff and pursued the evil spirits, beating them and driving them out of the country;
immediately, the pestilence was suddenly quelled.
Furthermore, he dreamed that powerful spirits and deities dug up the earth.
Sweet water welled up, filling all the fields;
consequently, the crops flourished and the five grains yielded in abundance.
Before a year had passed, the people were wealthy; this was taken as a sign of the year’s auspiciousness. 29.

The Response to Zhang Judo, Administrator of Wenzhou, Who Made a Vow to Produce Four Scrolls of the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-sūtra* While on the Dark Road: Case Twenty-Nine. Regarding the response to the vow made by Zhang Judo, Administrator of Wenzhou, to produce four scrolls of the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-sūtra* while on the dark road: [This is] from the *Chuan chumozui* (Biographies of the Extinction of Sin). Formerly, there was Zhang Judo, the Administrator of Wenzhou.
On account of the marriage of his daughter,
he slaughtered pigs, sheep, geese, ducks,
and other animals; less than ten days had passed.
He fell gravely ill and died;
after three nights, he revived and immediately explained the causes and conditions.
At first, he saw four people coming;
drawing a document from their bosoms, they showed it to Judo,
which was a joint petition by pigs, sheep, and others, stating:
Although pigs and other such beings have received animal bodies due to the accumulation of sins in previous lives,
they have their own natural life spans;
yet they are now forced to dwell upon the roads and are unjustly slaughtered one another.
After you have been judged, the Officer of Fate will dispatch a messenger to pursue you;
he will immediately bind you and take you away,
proceeding directly along a path toward the north.
When they reached the middle of the road, he sent someone to say:
"It is not yet fitting that I die;
by what skillful means might I seek a path to life?"
The litigants of the enemy faction numbered more than thirty heads;
they were stationed specifically at the base of the royal gate.
It was too late for regret.
Jujiao said,
"Reflecting upon my transgressions,
it is truly difficult to escape their consequences."
He asked for a single plan to bring about happiness.
The messenger said,
"You have killed living beings."
He made a vow to transcribe the four fascicles of the *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*,
believing that he would thereby escape all calamities;
immediately following this instruction, he recited those words once more.
After a short while, he looked toward the city gate and saw before the hall of Yama countless billions of people.
The sounds of lamentation and cries of pain were unbearable to hear.
He had the King of Singnam (Singing Name) perform music for the petition concerning the pigs and others;
he also recorded his vows while on the road.
The victim, riding upon this merit,
transformed his form according to his karma;
the King, filled with joy, returned once more to the path of rebirth.
Upon hearing these circumstances, more than one hundred people resolved to produce copies of the sutra;

This was the Dharma Master Ruihuī’s disciple;
he recited the Mahāyāna sūtras and remained motionless for an entire day and night.
As if having entered meditative concentration,
he opened his eyes again at dawn;
grief and joy welled up within him simultaneously.
Tears flowed and blood flowed with his sweat.
When the monk asked him the reason for this,
he replied:
"I have been invited to the palace of King Yama.
The king rose from his seat and spoke with reverence:
"Venerable sir, have you seen hell?
He replied, "I have heard its name,
but I have not yet seen its reality."
He then commanded the messenger to depart.
As he proceeded eastward in succession,
he beheld thirty-two great cities.
In each and every city,
there were hells;
among those undergoing suffering therein, the majority were śramaṇas.
Upon the rim of the iron cauldron,
there was a śramaṇa who preached the Dharma,
instructing, exhorting, benefiting, and gladdening them.
The sinner then asked:
"Who are you, sir,
that preaches the Dharma within this hell?"
The śramaṇa replied,
"I am the Bodhisattva Dhāraṇīśvararāja. Here,
within this Great Iron Ring of Mountains,"
There are immeasurable śramaṇas in hell who,
being greedily attached to worldly gain,
have violated the categories of the Buddha’s precepts.
They dwell together with the holy teachings in defiled monasteries,
lacking a sense of shame or remorse,
and they receive the offerings of the faithful in vain.
They preach the Dharma with impurity and delude the world;
such are their transgressions.
All have experienced the retributive fruits of hell.
Out of compassion for those śramaṇas who, through their folly, have summoned such suffering,
I [shall act] upon the rim of the cauldron.
Or, upon iron chariots,
they preach the Dharma according to their needs,
causing them to remember the karmic offenses they committed in the past.
I feel shame, repent, feel weary of the world, regret my transgressions,
and reproach myself. Having personally seen and heard these matters,
I am thus moved by both sorrow and joy.
Those who hear this find it difficult to differ;
those who reform their evils are indeed many. 40.
